description: Figure 5(b) is a line plot illustrating the ratio of training loss for several methods relative to the “Vanilla” baseline as a function of compute, expressed in FLOPs. The x-axis is labeled “FLOPs” and uses a logarithmic scale, with tick labels shown at approximately \(10^{17}\), \(10^{18}\), and \(10^{19}\) (no explicit unit beyond FLOPs). The y-axis is labeled “Loss Ratio” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from 0.94 up to 1.00 with regularly spaced tick marks at about 0.94, 0.96, 0.98, and 1.00. A purple solid line labeled “Vanilla” stays at a constant ratio of 1.00 across the entire FLOPs range. A blue solid line labeled “SepLLM (n=64)” starts near about 0.95 at the left edge (around \(10^{17}\) FLOPs), rises toward approximately 0.99 around the mid-to-right portion of the plot, and ends just under 1.00 near the right edge (around \(10^{19}\) FLOPs). A red solid line labeled “SepLLM (n=64,H/T)” begins lower (around 0.94–0.95 near \(10^{17}\) FLOPs), increases steadily, reaches about 0.99 by the midrange, and finishes close to 1.00 at the highest FLOPs. A green solid line labeled “SepLLM (n=128)” begins around 0.97 near \(10^{17}\) FLOPs, increases to approximately 1.00 around the middle of the x-range, and then remains near 1.00 through the right side. An orange solid line labeled “SepLLM (n=256)” starts around 0.98 near \(10^{17}\) FLOPs, rises to about 1.00 around the midrange, and stays near 1.00 toward \(10^{19}\) FLOPs.
